subject: history
title: Superpower, Civil Rights, Vietnam and Watergate
welcome_lead: From Pearl Harbor to Nixon's resignation: the United States as superpower at home and abroad.
meta_desc: A-Level adventure on WWII, the early Cold War, Civil Rights, Vietnam and Watergate 1972-74.
final_note: You can connect the rise of federal power to social transformation and the erosion of trust by 1975.

concepts.def: Japanese attack on the US Pacific Fleet at Hawaii on 7 December 1941, bringing the US into the Second World War.
Supreme Court ruling that 'separate but equal' public schooling was unconstitutional, overturning Plessy.
Lyndon Johnson's law outlawing racial discrimination in employment and public accommodations.
Federal statute banning literacy tests and authorising federal oversight of voter registration in the South.
Congressional authorisation for President Johnson to use military force in Vietnam following alleged North Vietnamese attacks.
Political scandal arising from the 17 June 1972 break-in at the DNC office; led to Nixon's resignation on 9 August 1974.

walkthroughs.body_html: Pearl Harbor (December 1941) ended isolationism. By 1945 the US wielded the atomic bomb and 50% of world GDP. The Truman Doctrine (March 1947), Marshall Plan (1948) and NATO (1949) shaped containment. McCarthyism (1950-54) and the Korean War (1950-53) deepened anti-communism. Eisenhower's 'New Look' relied on nuclear deterrence.

Brown (May 1954) catalysed activism; the Montgomery Bus Boycott (1955-56) and Little Rock (1957) followed. Sit-ins (1960) and Freedom Rides (1961) escalated pressure. The March on Washington (28 August 1963) and Birmingham forced Kennedy's bill. LBJ secured the Civil Rights Act (1964) and Voting Rights Act (1965). Watts (1965) and the assassination of Dr King (4 April 1968) revealed limits to legislative change.

The Gulf of Tonkin Resolution (August 1964) escalated US involvement; troop numbers peaked at 543,000 in 1969. The Tet Offensive (January 1968) shifted opinion. Nixon's 'Vietnamisation' and Paris Peace Accords (January 1973) brought withdrawal; Saigon fell in April 1975. The Watergate break-in (17 June 1972), the tapes and the impeachment process forced Nixon to resign on 9 August 1974.
